dimensions.label: Cheapest way to start
dimensions.a: Free is unlimited in pages and blocks for one person, so a real solo bill is $0
dimensions.b: Free Forever is $0 too, but its 60MB storage cap and one-time feature 'uses' push a real solo bill to $10 on Unlimited

dimensions.label: What the free plan really caps
dimensions.a: Blocks become 'limited' once a workspace has 2 or more members; Notion doesn't publish the number
dimensions.b: 60MB total file storage per Workspace, plus fixed one-time 'uses' for Custom Fields, Gantt, Timeline, Workload and Dashboards that never reset

dimensions.label: Core design center
dimensions.a: Pages and databases (subtasks, dependencies, custom properties) built for docs, wikis and light tracking
dimensions.b: Tasks first, with dedicated Gantt, Timeline, Workload and Dashboard views built for running day-to-day project work

dimensions.label: Built-in project-tracking views
dimensions.a: The pricing page lists no dedicated Gantt, Timeline or Workload view; databases add subtasks and dependencies instead
dimensions.b: Free Forever's own limits confirm Gantt, Timeline, Workload and Dashboards exist from the start, uncapped from Unlimited and Business

dimensions.label: Seat price for a 5-person team
dimensions.a: $60 a month on Plus ($12 a seat)
dimensions.b: $50 a month on Unlimited ($10 a seat)

dimensions.label: Seat price for a 15-person team
dimensions.a: $180 a month, still on Plus; no plan limit forces an upgrade at this size
dimensions.b: $285 a month, forced onto Business once Dashboards, Timeline and Workload views exhaust their 100-use-per-Workspace ceiling

dimensions.label: Where AI pricing lives
dimensions.a: Notion Agent, Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search are bundled into the $24 Business seat price
dimensions.b: Brain AI and Everything AI are separate per-member add-ons on top of any plan, at $14 or $33 a month

dimensions.label: Guests
dimensions.a: Free and unlimited on every paid plan; a guest opens only the pages they're invited to
dimensions.b: View-only guests are unlimited and free; permission-controlled guest seats are capped by a formula that scales with paid seats

dimensions.label: Importing the other tool's content
dimensions.a: No documented importer for ClickUp content; moving in means exporting and rebuilding by hand or with a third-party tool
dimensions.b: A built-in importer turns a Notion HTML export into ClickUp Lists and a nested Doc on every plan, though comments and attachments are dropped

dimensions.label: Admin and security controls
dimensions.a: SAML SSO and private teamspaces from Business; SCIM provisioning and an audit log are Enterprise-only and quote-priced
dimensions.b: Google SSO from Business; SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and an audit log are Enterprise-only and quote-priced

dimensions.label: Contract and commitment
dimensions.a: Month-to-month or yearly by choice on every plan, with no mixed-billing restriction stated
dimensions.b: Month-to-month or yearly by choice, but a Workspace can't mix monthly and yearly licenses, and switching to yearly means contacting support

verdicts.why: ClickUp's Spaces, Lists and multiple views handle several client projects and deadlines directly, and five seats cost less on ClickUp's Unlimited plan than on Notion's Plus plan.
Neither tool hosts lessons, sells a cohort or tracks student progress, so a course creator needs a platform built for that job instead of a wiki or a task board.

A Shopify store mostly needs a lightweight home for SOPs, supplier details and a content calendar, which fits Notion's page-and-database model at a lower cost before the store has enough staff to need Gantt charts or workload views.
Recurring job checklists, crew assignments and scheduling fit ClickUp's task-first views better than Notion's page-and-database model, and its per-seat price is also lower at a small team's size.

A freelancer with a short client list and no team to coordinate can run Notion's free plan at no cost, while ClickUp's free plan's storage and feature-use caps push a real solo bill onto its paid Unlimited plan.
ClickUp's sprint points and reporting on the Business plan target a product team's workflow directly, a feature neither of Notion's plans lists.
